match.reason: No point in the bank covers choosing between a standardised product and one customised for each market; the closest, on local, national and global businesses, only sorts businesses by where they operate.

draft.title: Standardisation and customisation
card: selling the same product, in the same form, in every market. One design and one process can be used everywhere, which usually lowers the cost of each item.
changing a product for each market. The changes may suit local tastes, meet local laws or respect local culture.
Examples of changes include a new flavour, different ingredients, a new size, different packaging or a translated label.
A business chooses where to sit between the two. It weighs the savings from selling one product against the extra sales that a better local fit may bring.
draft.remember: Standardised means the same product everywhere. Customised means changed to suit a market.

a.q: A snack company sells chips in Australia and Japan. In Japan it adds a local seaweed flavour. What is this?
opts: Customisation, as the product is changed for the market
Standardisation, as the same brand name is still used
Customisation, as the price is set below that of rivals
Standardisation, as the chips are made by the same company
a.why: The company changed the product to suit Japanese tastes, which is customisation. Keeping the same brand name does not make the product standardised, because the product itself is no longer the same in every market.
a.clue: Was the product itself changed for the market?

b.q: Dana's company sells the same phone charger in 40 countries. It changes only the plug type and the language in the manual to meet local rules. Which description fits best?
opts: Mostly standardised, with small changes to meet local needs
Fully standardised, as the product is the same everywhere
Fully customised, as each market gets its own design
Mostly customised, as every market has a different brand
b.why: The core charger is the same, so the product is mostly standardised. The plug and manual are changed to suit local rules, so it is not fully standardised. The wrong option that says fully standardised ignores these changes.
b.clue: Look at how much of the product stays the same, and what changes.

a.best: Customisation, as the product is changed for the market

b.best: Mostly standardised, with small changes to meet local needs
